text.tspan: SSH: two kinds of keys, and four ways to tunnel
Host key: the SERVER proves who it is
first connect: confirm the fingerprint → saved in
a man-in-the-middle) → REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!
User key: YOU prove you may log in
private key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 stays on your laptop;
the public key goes in the server's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
In AWS, prefer Systems Manager Session Manager or EC2 Instance Connect: no inbound port 22, no long-lived keys, sessions logged.
